research_problem: Whether Java libraries on Maven Central follow semantic versioning when introducing breaking changes, and how much breaking changes actually impact clients; the original Raemaekers study relied on an unsound tool and a 2011 snapshot
technical_approach: External differentiated replication: refined upgrade filters (semver-form, adjacent, external clients, Java-only, Java<=8), Maracas (japicmp-based) bytecode analysis computing binary breaking changes and affected client locations, applied to the original MDD (2011) and extended MDG (2018) corpora
primary_contribution: Large-scale replication overturning prior claims plus the Maracas BC/impact analysis tool
dataset_benchmark: 119,879 library upgrades and 293,817 clients from Maven Central (MDD 2011, MDG 2018)
evaluation_metrics: Share of breaking upgrades per semver level, temporal trend, share of broken clients; Maracas precision/recall on Jezek-Dietrich benchmark
key_findings: 83.4% of upgrades comply with semver but 20.1% of non-major upgrades break; non-major breaking upgrades fell from 67.7% (2005) to 16.0% (2018); only 7.9% of clients are impacted, most BCs touch unused declarations, but clients using them likely break; H3 of original study rejected; Maracas precision 96.3%, recall 98.5%
author_limitations: Tool imperfections (pessimistic); incomplete unstable-API conventions; library heuristic; qualified versions excluded; no version ranges; Java/MCR only; behavioural compatibility not studied
analyst_limitations: Binary-only BCs make 7.9% a lower bound; impact via static reachability not executed builds/tests; adjacent upgrades only; Java<=8 and data to 2018; not directly transferable to web APIs lacking compile-time checks
reproducibility: High: Zenodo package with code, notebooks and corpus access
suggested_extensions: REST/OpenAPI 'breaking bad' study combining spec diffs with consumer usage; behavioural BC detection via differential testing; checking LLM-generated code against library BCs; stability-marker standardisation; client reaction mining for migration
evidence_location: Protocol p.10-13; Maracas p.21-22; Q1 p.25-29; Q2 p.37; Q3 p.38-34; threats p.34-35; implications p.40-41; conclusion p.42
integrity: Several result tables column-split; trend figures missing; page markers out of order in Q3 section
